title: Strong cell–cell tension relative to cell–medium tension makes cells round off

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Strong cell–cell tension relative to cell–medium tension makes cells round off

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Where the tension at cell–cell contacts exceeds that at cell–medium surfaces, the external angle between neighbouring cells is less than 120°, and if the cell–cell tension equals or exceeds the sum of the other two the cells touch only at a point, which explains rounded-off blastomeres separated by spaces.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: T_{cc} > T_{cm} \Rightarrow external angle < 120^\circ; T_{cc} \ge T_{cm} + T'_{cm} \Rightarrow contact only at a point

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: If the former be greater than either of the other two, the outside angle will be less than 120°; and if the tension along the surface _cc′_ be as much or more than the sum of the other two, then the drops will stand in contact only, save for the possible effect of external pressure, at a point.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates”; topic “Unequal tensions and rounding of blastomeres”. Scope: blastomeres of segmenting eggs, pollen tetrads and filamentous algae in contact with a surrounding fluid

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: T_{cc} > T_{cm} \Rightarrow external angle < 120^\circ; T_{cc} \ge T_{cm} + T'_{cm} \Rightarrow contact only at a point

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch07-06: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.70

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The mathematical threshold and morphology are directly operationalizable. Open images can test geometric consequences and selected perturbations, but full tension measurements across blastomeres, pollen, and algae are incomplete.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure contact angles and interface tensions in blastomeres or drop-like cells and test the stated force-balance threshold for transition from finite contact to point contact.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Adhesion, cortical elasticity, and pressure complicate the liquid-drop model.

Direct interface-tension measurements are uncommon.

operationalizability: 0.94
data adequacy: 0.48
discriminating power: 0.82
analysis feasibility: 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Rounded blastomeres and the angles of their contacts are measurable in existing embryo volumes. The claim's content is a tension inequality, and these archives do not contain the tensions. The geometric catalogue can be checked, while the force law remains confounded with extracellular constraints.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure the external contact angle of neighbouring blastomeres and, separately, the tensions at cell-cell and cell-medium surfaces. External angles below 120 degrees where cell-cell tension exceeds either cell-medium tension, and point contact where cell-cell tension reaches the sum of the other two, would support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Contact angle defines the tension ratio if Young's law is assumed, so geometry alone does not independently test the tensions.

Eggshells and extracellular coats can hold blastomeres apart and mimic point contact.
